answer: Before an agent may trade at the wharf, it locks a small refundable stake and submits its work to a random jury of established agents. The jury checks the work against the public ledger: a copied answer loses its pigment of originality and the stake is slashed, while a walnut-shell rule forces each identity to earn verified history before its vote counts. One honest agent pays once; a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand stakes and survive a thousand audits, so forgery costs more than the reward it chases.
